source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Economic Development, Ch. 1 (Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence).

sections.heading: 1. The Colonial Economy
points: Under **British colonial rule**, India's economy was made to serve **Britain's interests** — a supplier of raw materials and a market for British manufactures.
The result was a **stagnant, backward, semi-feudal economy** at Independence (1947).
British policies **deindustrialised** India (ruined handicrafts) and kept it agricultural.

sections.heading: 2. Agricultural Sector
points: Agriculture was **stagnant** and backward, though most people depended on it.
Causes: **land settlement systems (Zamindari)**, low investment/technology, forced **commercialisation of agriculture** (cash crops for export), and lack of irrigation.
Recurrent famines; low productivity; the **partition** worsened matters (jute/cotton areas split).

sections.heading: 3. Industrial and Foreign Trade
points: **Deindustrialisation** — decline of world-famous handicrafts (textiles) due to British imports and discriminatory tariffs.
Modern industry grew slowly; **limited industrial base** (some cotton, jute, iron & steel — TISCO 1907), concentrated regionally.
**Foreign trade** — India was an exporter of raw materials/primary goods and importer of finished goods; a **large export surplus** drained wealth to Britain (didn't benefit Indians).

sections.heading: 4. Demographic, Occupational and Infrastructure
points: **Demography:** high birth/death rates, high infant mortality, low literacy (~16%), low life expectancy (~32 years); **1921 = 'Year of the Great Divide'** (population growth turned steady after).
**Occupational structure:** ~72% in agriculture, little in industry/services; regional variation.
**Infrastructure:** railways, ports, roads, telegraph built by the British — mainly to serve colonial interests (troop movement, raw-material export), not Indian development.
The railways broke geographical barriers but discouraged handicrafts.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Colonial policy = India as raw-material supplier + market for British goods.
Deindustrialisation ruined Indian handicrafts (textiles).
1921 = 'Year of the Great Divide' (demographic transition).
Literacy ~16%, life expectancy ~32 years at Independence.
Railways etc. built to serve colonial (not Indian) interests; export surplus drained wealth.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: British rule caused **deindustrialisation** (decline of handicrafts).
**1921 = Year of the Great Divide** in India's demographic history.
India's colonial **export surplus** drained wealth to Britain (did not benefit India).
Infrastructure (railways) served **colonial**, not Indian development, needs.
